note: Label values per 100 g or 100 mL exactly as the product record declares them. Nothing here is edited, rounded or filled in. Where a field is absent the label did not declare it, which is itself part of what the exercise tests. Barcodes let any reviewer pull the same record back.

edge.name: Peanut Butter
edge.why: On the US and European exchange lists a nut butter is a fat, not a protein, despite carrying 24 g of protein. If the fat list did not win outright this would come out as three protein exchanges.

edge.name: Μακεδονικό Ταχίνι με κακάο
edge.why: Sweetened tahini: a fat-list name carrying 32 g of carbohydrate, almost all of it added sugar. The fat gate has to hold on the energy share rather than on carbohydrate being absent.

edge.name: Ταχίνι Κακάο
edge.why: Same food declaring 0 g fibre, which is implausible for ground sesame. Tests that a stated zero does not swing the classification.

edge.name: Greek White panetto (vegan)
edge.why: Reads as a cheese, contains no protein at all: coconut oil and starch. The name must not be allowed to place it on the protein list.

edge.name: Figues moelleuses
edge.why: Dried fruit sits above the composition rule's carbohydrate ceiling, so it depends entirely on the name list. If the name is missed it lands on starch.

edge.name: Soft Figs
edge.ing: figs whole dried rehydrated, preservative: potassium sorbate
edge.why: Ingredients name a potassium salt that contributes no meaningful potassium. The additive scan must not flag potassium sorbate as a potassium source.

edge.name: Merenda
edge.why: Chocolate spread. Mostly sugar with 28 g of fat, so it must not read as fruit on the sugar fraction, and the fat must come out as separate fat exchanges.

edge.name: Coca-Cola Original
edge.ing: eau gazéifiée, sucre, colorant: E150d, acidifiant: acide phosphorique, arômes naturels
edge.why: Sugar water with no fibre declared and phosphoric acid in the ingredients. Tests that the fruit rule's fibre floor holds, that the drink reaches the sweets list rather than starch, and that the phosphate scan catches a French-worded acid. On starch it was charged 3 g of protein and 1 g of fat per exchange it does not have, which showed up as 46% energy drift.

edge.name: Goudse kaas oud 48+
edge.why: A high-fat protein: 20 g carries 5.2 g of protein and 6.6 g of fat, so one exchange has to be named high-fat and charged the fat the label declares rather than the list's nominal 8 g.

edge.name: Volkorenbrood
edge.why: The salt figure, 0.0024 g per 100 g, is not credible for bread and is almost certainly a crowd-sourced data error. Kept deliberately: it shows what an unverified database entry does to the sodium flag.
